page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine belonging to the Network Optimized family. It is equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The processor includes 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX (int8 and tile), and cryptographic acceleration extensions like AES and VAES.

The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not bundle local storage disks, requiring external network block storage for persistent data requirements. Acceleration hardware is not included, as the GPU count is zero. Benchmark data demonstrates exceptional single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core scores (2250.0), Geekbench text processing (2991.0), and single-threaded bzip3 decompression (15.23 GB/sec) ranking in the top tier. Compression pipelines also display elevated throughput, with single-threaded gzip achieving 34.94 GB/sec.

Multi-core execution and overall memory bandwidth test within median ranges, as evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 15831.29 and Redis throughput reaching 12.08 million operations per second. While small language model token generation reaches top-tier speeds at 348.78 tokens per second on 135M parameter models, larger 7B models reveal compute boundaries with generation speeds decreasing to 7.17 tokens per second. Cost efficiency centers around dense compute capability per core rather than total memory footprint or local storage inclusion. Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-8 is well aligned with compute-intensive tasks, batch compression, CI/CD compilation, and lightweight microservice serving.
